#### Ministry of Manpower — Employment requirements

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Public holiday entitlement and pay** (party in scope: Employee)
- **MOM rule explanation:** An Employment Act-covered employee has 11 paid public holidays each year. If a holiday falls on the rest day, the following working day will be a paid public holiday; if it falls on a non-working day, another day off or an extra day at the gross rate is due. Working on a public holiday ordinarily earns holiday gross pay plus an additional day at the basic rate; overtime applies beyond normal hours. By mutual agreement, the day may be substituted. Part IV coverage limits which employees may use time off in lieu. Distinguish a holiday on a working day, non-working day, or rest day. For holiday gross pay, the employee must not be absent without consent or reasonable excuse on the working day immediately before or after the holiday; authorised leave on either day is permitted. No holiday pay is due when the holiday itself falls during approved unpaid leave. Additional basic-rate pay is the default for working on the holiday; substitute-holiday arrangements require mutual agreement. An employee outside Employment Act coverage is governed by the contract. Time off in lieu of hours worked is available only to employees not covered by Part IV under the stated arrangement. Rest-day pay and any excess-hours overtime are separate entitlements. A case-specific conclusion requires: Employment Act and Part IV coverage. Work schedule and whether the date is a working, non-working or rest day. Whether the employee worked, hours worked, agreed substitution/time-off arrangements, and relevant absence or unpaid-leave facts. Does not decide a specific date’s gazetted holiday status or compute holiday pay without schedule and wage facts. Does not replace separate rest-day, overtime or part-time rules. [MOM | Public holidays: entitlement and pay](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/public-holidays-entitlement-and-pay)

sources.sourceText:
You are not entitled to holiday pay if the holiday falls on your approved unpaid leave.

If you are covered by the Employment Act, you are entitled to 11 paid public holidays in a year.

You are entitled to 11 paid public holidays a year in accordance with the Employment Act. If you are required to work on a public holiday, your employer should pay you an extra day’s salary or grant you off in lieu.

You were not absent on the working day immediately before or after a holiday without consent or a reasonable excuse.

You are on authorised leave (e.g. sick leave, annual leave, unpaid leave) on the day immediately before or after a holiday.

If the holiday falls on a rest day, the next working day will be a paid holiday.

If a public holiday falls on your rest day, the following working day will be a paid public holiday.

Public holidays falling on a rest day or non-working day

outcomes.question: Does MAS's LFMC compliance toolkit cover every return owed by the investment funds a licensed manager manages?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**MAS LFMC financial returns and SFA reporting requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** MAS’s 29 May 2026 SFA compliance toolkit states that an LFMC files quarterly Forms 1 and 2 within 14 days after each quarter end under Regulation 27 of the FMR. It also lists annual audited Forms 1 to 6 and the audited Profit and Loss Account, Balance Sheet and auditor’s report (including a management letter, if any) within five months after financial year end under section 107 of the SFA and Regulation 27 of the FMR. The toolkit says it is non-exhaustive and excludes obligations outside the SFA and fund-level requirements. Confirm the entity’s LFMC scope, reporting period, and current MAS-Tx instructions before applying these deadlines. A complete reporting calendar also needs the licence and manager regime, regulated activities, fund types and reporting periods, plus checks for event-triggered notifications and duties outside this toolkit. One quarterly financial return does not establish that all MAS duties are discharged. [LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit-lfmcs29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

**Source:** LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MAS LFMC financial returns and SFA reporting requirements): This compliance toolkit aims to provide LFMCs with a simple reference on the common applications, forms and submissions pursuant to the SFA that are applicable to LFMCs. However, it is not exhaustive, and LFMCs are expected to be familiar with all legislations and requirements that are applicable to them. For the avoidance of doubt, this toolkit excludes reporting obligations that fall outside the SFA; as well as fund-level requirements (e.g. Code of Collective Investment Scheme). Where an LFMC intends to apply for or holds a CMS licence to carry on business in other SFA regulated activities such as dealing in Capital Markets Products, it should also refer to the compliance toolkit that is relevant to these other types of regulated activities. outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**SFA 04-N24 reporting of misconduct by representatives from 1 January 2027** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** MAS Notice SFA 04-N24 takes effect on 1 January 2027. It applies to CMS licence holders and persons exempt under SFA section 99(1)(a)–(d), for misconduct by their representatives and former representatives. A CMI must submit a Misconduct Report no later than 21 calendar days after the date it first has reasonable grounds to believe the current or former representative committed misconduct during the representative period, unless the Authority allows a longer period in writing. Paragraph 21 keeps the cancelled Notice applicable where a report was submitted before 1 January 2027 or was required by 31 December 2026. Paragraph 20 addresses a pre-2027 reasonable-grounds case where no Misconduct Report in the form set out in the cancelled Notice had been submitted by 1 January 2027: the report under SFA 04-N24 is due within 21 calendar days after 1 January 2027, or a longer period allowed in writing. A case-specific conclusion requires the CMI status, representative period, reasonable-grounds date and transition facts. The notice’s stated commencement is 1 January 2027; this source does not establish what reporting duties applied before that date. sources.documentTitle: NOTICE ON REPORTING | OF MISCONDUCT OF
sources.sourceText:
1 | This Notice (excluding the Annexes) is issued pursuant to section 101(1) of the Securities and Futures Act 2001 ("the Act") and takes effect from 1 January 2027. Notice No. SFA 04-N11 issued on 26 November 2010 is cancelled with effect from 1 January 2027.

2 This Notice shall apply to all holders of a capital markets services ("CMS") licence and persons who are exempt from holding a CMS licence under section 99(1)(a), (b), (c) or (d) of the Act. It sets out the reporting requirements for the misconduct of their representatives and former representatives.

5 | If a CMI has reasonable grounds to believe that — (a) its representative had committed any misconduct; or Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives by Holders of Capital Markets Services Licence and Exempt Persons 3 (b) its former representative had committed any misconduct during the period when he or she was a representative of the CMI, the CMI must submit a Misconduct Report to the Authority, providing all the applicable information required therein in relation to the misconduct (called in this Notice "alleged misconduct"), no later than 21 calendar days, or such longer period as the Authority may allow in writing, after the date on which the CMI first has reasonable grounds to believe that which is mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) or (b).

20 Despite paragraph 5, where a CMI — (a) first had reasonable grounds to believe, before 1 January 2027, that any type of misconduct within the definition of "misconduct" in paragraph 3 of this Notice was committed by its representative or its former representative when he or she was its representative; and (b) has not submitted to the Authority a Misconduct Report, which is in the form set out at Appendix 1 of the Notice on Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives by Holders of Capital Markets Services Licence and Exempt Financial Institutions (MAS Notice No. SFA 04-N11) (" Cancelled Notice "), in relation to the misconduct before 1 January 2027, the CMI must submit to the Authority a Misconduct Report in relation to the misconduct under this Notice and any other document or information that may be required under paragraphs 6 to 8 of this Notice, no later than 21 calendar days, or such longer period as the Authority may allow in writing, after 1 January 2027.

21 This Notice does not apply to or in relation to any of the following, and despite paragraph 1, the Cancelled Notice as in force immediately before 1 January 2027 continues to apply to or in relation to any of the following as if this Notice has not been issued: (a) any case for which a CMI submitted a Misconduct Report under the Cancelled Notice (which is in the form set out at Appendix 1 of that Notice) before 1 January 2027; (b) any case for which a CMI was required under the Cancelled Notice to submit a Misconduct Report (which is in the form set out at Appendix 1 of that Notice) by 31 December 2026, save that a reference in the Cancelled Notice to "MASNET" is to MASNET or any electronic system which may be established by the Authority in place of MASNET.
